subject.title: Feishu: bot does not respond when @-mentioned in a reply message

question: Should maintainers repair/adopt the conflicting cross-repo Feishu reply-mention candidate, or close that candidate and allow a new narrow OpenClaw PR for this issue?
rationale: The issue is valid at source level, but the direct same-repo PR is closed unmerged and the remaining open candidate is outside the target repo, conflicting, not maintainer-editable, and based on a branch with prior routing and mention-gating concerns.

options.title: Replace with a narrow current-main PR
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting candidate, then allow a focused Feishu fix that keeps mention detection and root routing scope-aware with real Feishu proof.

options.title: Adopt and repair the existing candidate
options.body: A maintainer can bring the existing head into an OpenClaw branch, address the prior findings, and attach redacted real behavior proof before review.

options.title: Keep waiting on the candidate
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the cross-repo PR, accepting that it is currently conflicting and cannot be directly modified by OpenClaw maintainers.

recommendation.title: Replace with a narrow current-main PR
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the conflicting candidate, then allow a focused Feishu fix that keeps mention detection and root routing scope-aware with real Feishu proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman merged the adjacent Feishu reply-targeting, topic routing, and replyInThread changes most relevant to the adoption-or-replacement decision.
